method: Each of the 41 rows was read at source. A row is VERIFIED only when every file in its declared corpus implements its own capability; CORRECTED when the corpus contained another row's implementation; PARTIALLY RECONSTRUCTED when the capability is a region of a shared file or extends beyond the measured corpus. Line counts are splitlines() of the audit tree; class counts use the same patterns as the register's generator.

rows.title: Platform KPI dashboard (users, resumes, applications, AI generations, storage)
rows.rationale: The directory holds exactly one file, dashboard.jsx (507 L, 6 useState / 3 useEffect / 1 API import). There is no other capability in the corpus to contaminate it.

rows.title: Subsystem health catalogue (28 services, latency, remediation hints)
rows.rationale: Three files, all health-specific: PlatformHealth (372 L, 61 capability-term hits), ApiHealthMatrix (263 L) and ServiceDetailPanel (244 L) are the catalogue, the matrix and the detail panel of one screen. No other row claims them.

rows.title: Security event stream / audit viewer
rows.rationale: The declared corpus was AdminAuditLogs.jsx (398 L) + PlatformSecurity.jsx (362 L). AdminAuditLogs.jsx IS the whole corpus of FP-A22 (dedicated audit-log browser) and contains no security-event stream; including it credited this row with another row's implementation. The row's own endpoints (/platform/security-events) resolve to getSecurityEvents in PlatformSecurity.jsx, which is therefore the whole scoped corpus.

rows.title: Operator roster + force-revoke sessions
rows.rationale: One file, PlatformOperators.jsx, 769 L with 17 useState hooks and a platformApi import; it is the operator roster itself, not a wrapper.

rows.title: IP blocklist / deny rules
rows.rationale: The row claims an IP blocklist / deny rules. Its declared corpus (PlatformSecurity.jsx, 362 L) contains no blocklist, deny rule or IP-ban logic: a case-insensitive search of the whole legacy tree for blocklist/deny-rule/IP-ban vocabulary returns only an unrelated hit in Checkout.jsx. The register's own evidence cites `handleBlockIp`, which exists ONLY in the MODERN file frontend/src/components/admin/AdminSecurityTab.tsx:214. The legacy corpus therefore implements FP-A05's security-event stream, not this row's capability: the legacy side has NO implementation, and the MOCK/FABRICATED finding is a modern-side finding.

rows.title: Marketing content: phrases, reviews, trusted-by logos, landing pages
rows.rationale: Four files, each one of the four things the row claims (phrases 246 L, reviews 432 L, trusted-by 101 L, admin landing pages 344 L). No other row claims them.

rows.title: At-risk attention inbox / platform insights
rows.rationale: One file, PlatformAttention.jsx, 130 L with 8 useState hooks and one API import: small but genuinely the attention inbox, not a wrapper.

rows.title: Employer application + job posting moderation
rows.rationale: Two files, one per half of the row's own title (employer applications 585 L, jobs manager 599 L with 179 capability-term hits).

rows.title: Platform tenant registry (list tenants, quotas, suspend)
rows.rationale: One file, PlatformTenants.jsx, 2,105 L with 312 capability-term hits — the tenant registry in full.

rows.title: Company management (verification, documents, quotas)
rows.rationale: One file, CompanyManagement.jsx, 641 L with ZERO useState, ZERO useEffect and ZERO API calls — a static fixture screen. That is precisely why the row is MOCK/FABRICATED; the corpus is correct and the classification is supported by the absence of data plumbing.

rows.title: User manager, User360 drawer, session revoke
rows.rationale: Four files that together are user management: UsersManager (1,013 L), User360Drawer (1,513 L), UserEdit (469 L), CreateUserModal (244 L). FP-A18's bulk operations are a region inside UsersManager, so this parent corpus is correct for its own scope; the overlap is declared rather than removed.

rows.title: Bulk user operations (multi-select, bulk role change, bulk removal)

regions.what: multi-selection state, select-all, bulk suspend/remove handlers

rows.rationale: The capability is a REGION of UsersManager.jsx (selection state 34-50, select-all 155-170, bulk handlers 328-430), not three whole files. The published corpus also carried User360Drawer (1,513 L) and CreateUserModal (244 L), neither of which implements a bulk operation. A line-region measurement is stated rather than a file count, because a bulk action is not a whole-file property; the file-level number below is the containing file.

rows.title: Job queues, DLQ, outbox, cache, backups (operations console)
rows.rationale: The declared corpus was five files across four directories. Two of them (command/, 381 L) are the whole corpus of FP-A23 (command palette + entity search) and one (sidebar.jsx, 538 L) is the corpus of FP-A26 (console shell and tab routing). Neither implements queues, DLQ, outbox, cache or backups. The scoped corpus is PlatformQueues (379 L) + PlatformOperations (332 L) = 711 L.

rows.title: Dedicated audit-log browser with filters and export
rows.rationale: One file, AdminAuditLogs.jsx, 398 L with 94 capability-term hits and the row's own endpoints (/admin/audit-logs, /admin/audit-logs/stats). It is the audit browser itself.

rows.title: Admin command palette + entity search
rows.rationale: Two files that are exactly the palette and its search engine (AdminCommandPalette 239 L, adminEntitySearch 142 L). The palette imports searchPlatform from platformApi, matching the row's own implementation.

rows.title: Public pricing, plan comparison and checkout
rows.rationale: Three files, one per element the row names: Plans (1,123 L), PlansTable (206 L), Checkout (2,524 L). No other row claims them.

rows.title: 71 modular portfolio page blocks (About1-6, Experience1-2, Education1-2, Contact1-4, Awards1-2, …)
rows.rationale: 72 files: 71 category/block components plus index.js, which re-exports NavbarCategory, HeroCategory, AboutCategory … AwardsCategory. That is one block library, which is what the row claims. The 72nd file is an export barrel, not a second capability.

rows.title: Public portfolio rendering + slug availability + publish
rows.rationale: One file, PublicPortfolio.jsx, 307 L with 114 capability-term hits and 4 useState hooks.

rows.title: Portfolio template gallery with palettes
rows.rationale: Seven files: four named templates (CreativeDark, Executive, ModernMinimal, PremiumTech), shared.jsx, WebCvRenderer.jsx and index.js. All are the template gallery; the shared helpers are part of it rather than a separate capability.

rows.title: Portfolio gallery / showcase
rows.rationale: One file, PortfolioGallery.jsx, 238 L with 6 useState hooks and 85 capability-term hits.

rows.title: Interview session UI (question flow, transcript, scoring)
rows.rationale: Six files that are one interview session: DashboardInterviews (3,129 L), LiveInterviewSession (1,691 L), LiveAnswerGuide (281 L), LiveAudioWaveform (254 L), LiveResumeDrawer (229 L) and LiveVoiceEngine (233 L). FP-D01 and FP-D02 measure the voice delivery and microphone sub-capabilities, whose implementation is INSIDE this session — a session UI cannot have a voice mode without containing it. The sharing is real and the corpus is correct for the session, but this row's subfeature counts include those two sub-capabilities' classes and must be read with that in mind.

rows.title: Dashboard-v2 element library (stats, activity, profile display, resumes/covers lists)
rows.rationale: The 28-file corpus mixed dashboard elements with the CONTENT-MARKETING homepage: 13 files under Dashboard2/elements are HomepageHero, HomepageFooter, HomepagePricing, HomepageReviews, Homepagefaqs, HomepageTemplates and siblings. Those same files are the implementation of FP-G10 (CMS custom pages / landing-page rendering), so they were counted twice and this row's element library was inflated with marketing copy it does not own. The scoped corpus keeps the Dashboard widgets, the AppShell and the shared common/ widgets.

rows.title: Candidate shell, AI career briefing, top job matches, executive rail, progress charts
rows.rationale: The 16-file Candidate directory contains three independent capabilities with their own rows: CubaNextSteps (FP-D10, onboarding checklist), PaymentGraceBanner + gracePeriodNotice (FP-D14, dunning banner) and candidateEntitySearch (candidate search). The shell is correctly composed of them at runtime, but counting their classes as the shell's own measurement contaminates it.

rows.title: Saved jobs / favourites
rows.rationale: One file, DashboardFavourites.jsx, 401 L with 7 useState hooks.

rows.title: Guided multi-step resume builder (Form/Boards/Actions steps)
rows.rationale: The builder legitimately spans four directories (61 files), and the step components are its own implementation. It also contains whole sub-capabilities with their own rows — ATS meter (FP-E04/E05), AI writing aids (FP-E10), import/sync modals, template selection (FP-E08's share entry point) — so a single scoped file set would be arbitrary. The ATS meter is excluded here because it is a self-contained measured capability; the remaining overlap is declared and the row needs per-step scoping before its subfeature table is cited as its own.

rows.title: Public share links / share modal

regions.what: share state, plan-gated handleShare, review-link modal mounts

rows.rationale: The capability is a share modal, but the row was measured over the ENTIRE BuildResume directory (36 files, 16,941 L) — the same corpus as FP-E01's builder. The implementation is Dashboard/ShareModal/ShareModal.jsx (270 L) plus a handful of share handlers inside BuildResume.jsx. A 36-file corpus for a share modal is the same defect class as FP-A08's 68-file directory.

rows.title: Cover letters
rows.rationale: 74 declared files: the entire cv-templates directory (72 files) plus CoverLetter.jsx. cv-templates is the corpus of FP-E02/FP-E03 (template catalogue volume and diversity) and CoverLetter.jsx does not read it — it imports ../TemplateRenderer, a single shared renderer. Including 72 unrelated template files inflated the cover-letter row by an order of magnitude.

rows.title: Smart resume layout engine (section partitioner, 5 layouts, themed rendering)
rows.rationale: 23 files that are one engine: SmartResumeComposer, 14 Smart* section components, 5 layouts, smartPartitioner, themePresets and 2 utils. That is exactly the partitioner + layouts the row claims.

rows.title: Export access guard (plan-gated export routes)
rows.rationale: Three files, all export access: Exporter (104 L), RequireExportAccess (30 L), exportAccess.js (42 L) — guard, gate and component.

rows.title: Regional job hubs / landing pages
rows.rationale: Four files, all regional job landing pages (JobsLanding, JobsLandingHero, LandingJobTopCompanies, LandingJobsFeatured). FP-F10 includes this directory but that is FP-F10's contamination, not this row's.

rows.title: Job listing browse/filter UI (beyond maps and autocomplete)
rows.rationale: The row claims browse/filter (FP-F07 separately claims maps and autocomplete). Its corpus included the whole JobsLanding directory, which is FP-F08's entire declared corpus — four regional hub pages with no listing filters. Scoped to JobsListings (17 files).

rows.title: Employer dashboard: companies management, job editing, application modals, rejection reasons
rows.rationale: Seven files that are one employer dashboard: EmployerDashboard (720 L), CompaniesManagement (566 L), AddCompanyModal (591 L), EditCompany-replacement EditJobModal (713 L), JobApplicationsModal (576 L), RejectionReasonModal (107 L) and SendMessageDialog (114 L). Every file serves the row's own title. The sharing is justified in both directions: the messaging dialog is FP-F03's implementation, and this directory is where M8C found the real implementations of FP-F05/FP-F06, whose own declared corpora were 25- and 27-line wrappers.

rows.title: Cuba design-system primitives (30 components)
rows.rationale: 52 files: 30+ design-system primitives AND five feature components whose capabilities have their own rows (candidate command palette, copilot mascot, HUD, density provider, application shell). A component library legitimately ships composite components, so the corpus is not wrong — but this is sharing, not independent verification: the row's subfeature counts include those five features' classes, which is why it is recorded as a justified share rather than a clean measurement. Excluding them would be defensible too; the choice is stated so a reader can take the other one.

rows.title: Toast / notification feedback primitives
rows.rationale: One file, Toats.jsx (131 L, 0 useState, 0 API) — presentational toast primitives. The filename is misspelt in the legacy tree; that is a naming defect, not a corpus defect.

rows.title: Blog authoring + public blog
rows.rationale: Seven files: BlogEditor (1,631 L), BlogList (387 L), BlogPost (483 L), BlogCard (171 L), CategoryFilter (84 L), BlogManagement (874 L), BlogPreviewModal (281 L). Authoring and the public blog are the row's own two halves.

rows.title: CMS custom pages / landing page rendering
rows.rationale: 17 files: CustomePage.jsx (299 L), LandingPage.jsx and 15 Marketing/elements sections. The row claims CMS custom pages and landing-page rendering; the elements ARE the landing page. FP-D12 also counted them, which is D12's contamination, corrected there.

rows.title: Marketing site: welcome, features, FAQ, about, contact, legal
rows.rationale: Welcome (1,504 L), Features (667 L) and Contact (420 L) are genuinely one marketing surface, so the corpus is not contaminated. But the row's stated scope includes FAQ/about/legal pages that live in another row's directory, so the capability is only partly covered by the measured corpus. Reconstructing it means deciding whether those pages are part of this row or of FP-G10 — a register-level decision, not a measurement.
missingEvidence: FAQ, About and Legal content is NOT in this corpus. A search of the three files for FAQ returns zero hits; FAQ content exists in Marketing/elements/Homepagefaqs.jsx and faqData.js, which belong to FP-G10's corpus. The row's title overstates what the corpus implements.

rows.title: Shared utility library (42 modules: formatting, validation, download, OAuth resolvers, print)
rows.rationale: 43 files of shared utilities. Other rows measure individual modules of this library as their own implementation, which is what a utility library is for; the sharing is therefore justified and recorded. It is not independent verification of this row: its counts are the union of everything in src/utils, including capabilities measured elsewhere.

rows.title: Data models, runtime conf and React context scaffolding
rows.rationale: Seven files: four models (Education, Employment, Language, Skills), two conf modules and AuthContext. src/models contains exactly those four files, so the corpus is complete for what it claims.

rows.title: Cross-cutting hooks (unread pollers, AI token usage, AI engine status, service availability, dialogs)
rows.rationale: 11 hook modules. Hooks are cross-cutting by construction and other rows consume them; being used by several capabilities is their purpose, so the sharing is justified. As with the other library rows, the counts describe the library, not an isolated capability.

rows.title: In-app support surface and input validation modals
rows.rationale: The row claims the in-app support surface and input-validation modals. DashboardToast is neither: DashboardSupport.jsx does not import it (a grep for DashboardToast inside DashboardSupport returns nothing), and its subject is toast notification primitives, which is FP-G07's capability. Scoped to DashboardSupport (916 L) + ValidationModal (438 L).
